[`bun build --compile --aot`](/bundler/aot-adoption) holds values to their TypeScript types. The type checker lets an `any` go anywhere, so the compiler checks it when the program runs: at the variable, parameter, property or return type that it reaches first. A value that does not match throws a `TypeError` there.

This rule reports each of those places. Every report is a check that can throw. An `any` that goes into another `any`, into `unknown`, or into a variable without a type is not checked and not reported.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. This rule needs types, so turning it on makes `bun lint` type check your code first.

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"bun/aot-no-any-to-typed" = "error" # or "warn"
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 3} */}
```ts
interface User {
  id: number;
  name: string;
}
declare function greet(user: User): string;

declare const text: string;
const body = JSON.parse(text);
const id: number = body.id;
greet(body);

function nameOf(): string {
  return body.name;
}
```

A value stored in a typed array, `Map` or `Set` is checked when it is read back:

{/* bad */}
```ts
declare const text: string;
const body = JSON.parse(text);
const ids: number[] = [];
ids.push(body.id);
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```ts
declare const text: string;
const body = JSON.parse(text);
const copy = body.id;
const later: unknown = body.id;
console.log(body, String(body.id));
```

Check the value once, where it comes in. After that it has a type:

{/* good */}
```ts
declare function double(n: number): number;

declare const text: string;
const body: unknown = JSON.parse(text);
if (typeof body !== "number") throw new Error("expected a number");
double(body);
```

## How it relates to `no-unsafe-*`

[`@typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-argument`](/lint/rules/typescript/no-unsafe-argument), [`no-unsafe-assignment`](/lint/rules/typescript/no-unsafe-assignment) and [`no-unsafe-return`](/lint/rules/typescript/no-unsafe-return) also report an `any` that goes nowhere in particular, such as `const copy = body.id`. They do not report `yield body.id`, `total ||= body.id` or an `any` inside an array literal that is an argument. This rule reports exactly what `--aot` checks.

Where this rule is on, they leave to it the places that it reports, so you see each place once. They do so only if this rule is at least as severe as they are: where one of them is an error and this rule is a warning, you see both, and the error stays an error. A comment that disables this rule at a place silences the place.
